description: We are Leidy & Co., a team of Software Technology Engineering students with varied tastes and a lot of curiosity about technology. We are passionate about video games, movies, music, comics, and anything that gives us an excuse to learn or create something new. We believe that with creativity, curiosity, and a computer, we can go pretty far.
summary:
Neek turns NASA and ESA satellite data into clear decisions for the field. A farmer in Yucatán uploads or pastes their plot and, within seconds, sees it over cloud-free Sentinel-2 imagery. They discover where their land has more vegetation, chlorophyll, moisture or exposed soil, pixel by pixel, and compare it with rainfall (GPM), soil moisture (SMAP), temperature (MODIS) and evaporation (MERRA-2).

Neek' then suggests three crop rotations tailored to their soil and climate, with or without a planting history. Each one explains why it is recommended, what gains it can bring and what to check in the field.

It matters because a good rotation protects the soil, saves water and safeguards the harvest against droughts and extreme rain. Neek puts that advantage, today reserved for those with technical advice, in the hands of any farmer, using only open data.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

Smallholder farmers in Yucatán have to decide what to plant, when, and what to rotate it with, but the satellite and climate data that could guide them are scattered across many sources and hard to read. .Neek' brings that data together in one place. A farmer opens a satellite map of Yucatán, outlines their field (by clicking its corners, uploading a GeoJSON file or pasting coordinates) and picks a planting month. In seconds, .Neek' returns ranked recommendations for 8 crops with a clear traffic-light verdict and the exact limiting factors (soil pH, texture, rainfall, heat exposure), plus up to 3 multi-season rotation plans scored for soil health, water savings and pest-cycle breaking. It also overlays satellite and climate layers on the field's exact outline: NASA SMAP soil moisture, Sentinel-2 plant health (NDVI at about 10 m) and its change over 30, 60 or 90 days, 30-day rainfall and dry streaks, evapotranspiration, and soil pH, carbon and cation-exchange capacity. Every finding comes with the evidence behind it and a suggested action, and results can be read aloud. Under the hood, NASA POWER supplies the daily climate history for the field's own location, ISRIC SoilGrids supplies soil properties, and FAO ECOCROP supplies crop requirements. A transparent, editable scoring engine combines them, so every recommendation can be traced and explained.

BENEFITS

Farmers get better planting decisions based on real climate history and soil data for their own field, using free open data and no sensors or subscriptions. .Neek' makes NASA, Sentinel-2 and ISRIC data accessible to people who could never use them through technical tools. Its rotation plans protect the land by encouraging crop diversity and water savings. It also stays honest: every result carries a data-confidence rating kept separate from the suitability score, and when a data source is missing .Neek' says so instead of guessing. The interface is bilingual (Spanish/English), with adjustable text size and voice reading, so it reaches people who are not comfortable with dense dashboards.

INTENDED IMPACT

We want to put data-driven planning in the hands of the people who need it most. .Neek' aims to help Yucatán's farmers reduce crop failures caused by unsuitable crop or timing choices, use water more wisely in a region with heavy seasonal rain and long dry spells, build soil health through smarter rotations, and adapt to a changing climate using long-term observed data instead of rules of thumb that are shifting under their feet. Because it is built on global open data (NASA, ESA Sentinel-2, ISRIC, FAO), the same approach can be extended to other regions and countries.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES, HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE

Languages: Python for the backend and analysis; JavaScript, HTML and CSS for the web app. Backend: FastAPI and Uvicorn on an Oracle Cloud server behind nginx. Geospatial stack: Shapely, rasterio, Fiona, pyproj and NumPy for polygon validation, raster clipping and pixel-level analysis. Satellite data: pystac-client and Microsoft Planetary Computer for Sentinel-2 L2A imagery, with cloud, shadow and water masking. Frontend: Leaflet with Esri World Imagery as the satellite basemap. Data sources: NASA POWER (daily climate), NASA GIBS SMAP L4 (soil moisture), ESA Sentinel-2 (vegetation), ISRIC SoilGrids (soil), FAO ECOCROP (crop requirements), INEGI soil maps (depth indicators) and Meteomatics (optional cross-check). Quality: a pytest suite covers the engine, API, rotations and data layers. Hardware: no special hardware is needed. It runs on a standard cloud server, and farmers only need a browser.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

First, it joins data sources that normally live apart. NASA, ESA, ISRIC, FAO and INEGI data meet in one workflow around a single field outline. Second, transparency is a design principle: every score is explainable, the tool separates "how suitable is this crop" from "how good is the evidence", it never fills in missing data, and it openly labels each layer's real resolution. Third, it offers rotation intelligence rather than a simple crop list, planning sequences across seasons and using crop families to break pest cycles. Fourth, it is designed for real farmers: their own declarations (previous crop, rainfed or irrigated, priorities) change the results, and voice reading plus a bilingual interface lower the barrier to use. Finally, it has its own visual identity, with a brand and iconography rooted in Yucatán.

FACTORS OUR TEAM CONSIDERED

Scientific honesty: we deliberately avoided overselling. .Neek' is an explainable heuristic engine, not a yield forecast, and we state what each layer can and cannot tell a farmer. Data reliability: we account for the publication delays of NASA POWER and Sentinel-2, and use local caching and incremental updates so the tool stays fast and never overwrites its original historical data. Accessibility: bilingual text, scalable fonts and voice reading serve a mixed-literacy audience. Input validation: polygons are checked for location inside Yucatán, edge crossings, area and coordinate order, so bad input never produces bad advice. Responsible data use: we keep provider attributions and licenses visible. Cost and scalability: open data, a lightweight server and a browser-only client keep .Neek' affordable to run and easy to extend. Next steps: effective soil depth, nutrient data, per-field climate grids and field-validated calibration with local agronomists.
